## Data analysis

### Looking at specialisms alignment with the scenarios

::: callout-caution
## Demo only

This is a visualization for demonstrative purposes:
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-alignment-scenarios
#| fig-title: "Alignment indices by scenario and Specialism"
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-align: "center"
alignment_scenarios_long |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = id, y = alignment_index)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~Specialism) +
  labs(y = "Alignment index", x = "Scenarios") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust=1))
```

### Questions for Viz

NB here we are looking at how well specialisms (including combinations of specialisms) are aligned with the scenarios people told us about. Before we were looking at how well people’s own profiles were aligned with the specialisms.

1.  The main thing is the kind of analysis that we sketched out in the slide above. Those two graphs show comparative views of the scenarios based on how the alignment changes when you are combining specialisms in greater numbers. Carlos and I were chatting about this last week and he said we might be able to do an interactive view of these to help explore the qualitative dataset (I.e. click on a specific point or line and it would tell you what the scenario number or name is, and then can look at the description). In the report we might just need to highlight a small number that are being referred to specifically, rather than necessarily embedding an interactive visualisation (which wouldn’t work well for a pdf/print version).

To make these graphs, there are csv files for 'max_alignment_scenarios_1_permutations', all the way up to 5 permutations. These are generated via the alignment_metric script.

One aspect of the data that we are losing here is: we are only looking at the categories of expertise that are included in CyBOK, and ignoring the additional categories that we added in. So one or two of them have very high alignment (17 and 23 for instance), but this is because these scenario were dominated by non-CyBOK categories of expertise, and the CyBOK ones had low values. To illuminate where this is the case, perhaps we could colour code the data points on the scatter to signal the fraction of expertise that was under CyBOK? This should be easy as it is just (sum of 'response' for that ID in 'comb_scenario' dataframe / sum of numeric fields for that ID in 'scenarios' dataframe, excluding the ID field itself)
:::
